plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms, from pompons to spiders. It thrives in the cooling temperatures and shortening days of fall and is widely grown in gardens and as a cut flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide, especially East Asia, Europe, and North America
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are short-day plants, so they set buds only when nights grow long enough. The flower is a national symbol of Japan, and the Imperial Seal is a stylized chrysanthemum.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall native wildflower with daisy-like flowers that have purple rays and yellow centers. It brightens meadows, roadsides and prairies late in the season and is an important nectar source for migrating monarch butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (August to October)
plants.funFact: Its flowers close at night and on cloudy days, and the plant is a key fuel stop for monarch butterflies migrating to Mexico.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular tree covered in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers that carpet the ground beneath it. It blooms before its fernlike leaves fully emerge, creating a purple haze over streets and parks in the Southern Hemisphere spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring (October to November in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City' because of its roughly 70,000 jacaranda trees, which turn the city purple every October.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: A graceful annual with feathery foliage and saucer-shaped flowers on slender stems. It flowers prolifically until the first frost and is a favorite of pollinators and cut-flower gardeners.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer through first frost (to October or later in mild climates)
plants.funFact: The name 'cosmos' comes from the Greek word for 'order' or 'harmony,' which Spanish priests in Mexico applied to the plants' orderly petals.
